Golden standard for what a remaster should be. More or less rebuilt from the ground up as if its a new game based off the standards we expect today, not just slapping some new textures on old assets and shipping it.

A bottle of the classic Silent Hill formula mixed with analog horror, insane sound design and visuals.

It gives off strong Sam Barlow’s "SH: Shattered Memories" vibes in the best sense possible. Expect a deep, heavy atmosphere of despair, isolation, and infinite guilt that you just can't easily shake off.

In 1998, Half-Life, a game which would redefine the first-person shooter, was released.
Six years later, in 2004, its sequel, Half-Life 2, released. It sent ripples through gaming as it was known then, revolutionizing graphics, story, and physics.

In 2013, Garfield Kart came out. A masterpiece in its own right, tackling tough themes like war, horror, and anime.
Six years later, it was succeeded by Garfield Kart - Furious Racing, whose impact would be double its predecessor.
I'm not saying there is pattern to things, but this game is certainly Microids's magnum opus.

Few games come as close to perfection as this game.

The sound design is absolutely crisp, animations satisfying and gameplay truly amazing. Moving and mantling in this game are as smooth as butter and control fabulously. The only downsides that come to mind are the incredibly repetitive dialogue of the two guys in your earpiece during frontier defense. They probably cycle through about 4 different lines at the end of every wave and beginning of every game. It becomes annoying very fast. This can of course be fixed by killing the dialogue audio slider, but I digress.

Definitely pick up this game on sale or even full price if you're feeling it. It's worth it.

Feels a lot tighter and more polished than the previous game. Less filler, more action. The elemental powers and enemy strength/weakness to then give you a reason to try new armor and weapon combos. The story feels "less good" than the previous one, like there's just less of it since most of what you do is restore your castle and than go fight the final boss. The mini-quests aren't very interesting - just go kill something. But overall it was fun and felt better than the first one in terms of pacing and gameplay. And Geralt's narration is always welcome.

Great game, fantastic game, if you can get it working. A 20 year old game has no reason to be missing half of it's entire audio library. Condemned: Criminal Origins has existed on Steam for 20 years and collected revenue as an incomplete product.

A neat little game that was a delight to play every second of the way. 

It's not groundbreaking by any means. Just a well crafted top down metroidvania starring cute ghost animals. The story is simple but features some effective emotional bits. I guess the one thing I could nitpick is that there isn't much context for many things in the world and they are just there. But they are cool set pieces either way.

Gameplay is solid, with a simple but effective moveset, a system of equippable perks and fun enemy and boss encounters. 

Honestly, the biggest flaw is that I wish the game was longer. It took around 12 hours on hard mode, Though, it's only a flaw because of how much I enjoyed my time with it. I wouldn't mind if there were more things to find and some extra side quests to hang out with your friends more. 

Overall: 8.5/10

I have mixed feelings on this game. I feel that it had a lot of potential that it didn't reach. Interesting story and plot twists, but some things are spoon-fed to you and other things seem impossible to discover without a walk-through. Very repetitive gameplay because of the time-loop, which I'm sure is intentional, but could have been executed better. Certain times it allows you to skip dialogue, even if you haven't seen it yet, but other times there will be long cutscenes and waiting periods that you can't skip. There are so many options and yet so many will just end the same way. I feel there could have been so much more to this game.

An incredible experience made all the more incredible because I went into this game totally blind and had no idea about the companions. I thought that really lovely person who was helping me not get my butt kicked / lost was an AI. Stranger, I have no idea who you are, but you're the most generous, patient human being alive. I literally got up and left my computer for several minutes multiple times (sorry!!), and you just patiently waited for me to return. I've never had a more awe-inspiring and mortifying experience than when I went googling this game afterward and cried out "that was a PERSON?!". 

Anyway, fantastic social experience. Really looking forward to playing again.
